authority: Proposed permanent governing specification; not approved until the user explicitly approves it. Once approved, implementation must conform. Amendments require explicit user approval and a recorded versioned change.

canon.setting: Fictional sovereign city-state named Saltwater; one city and one sovereign jurisdiction only.
canon.world: No external playable cities, territories, or expansion. External places may exist only as off-map references when needed for trade, travel, origins, or case context.

population.counting: Every living person is counted exactly once, including police, officials, visitors who qualify as resident population, and all other people defined by the population rules.
population.rule: The 500 reserve is headroom, not a second population. Entries consume available headroom; deaths and permanent exits release capacity. Never exceed 10,000 living persons.

police.scope: Primary deepest simulation; every employee individually persistent and operationally represented.

canon.interface: Text-first permanently. Extensive detailed narrative, records, reports, dialogue, evidence and chronology are core gameplay. Maps and selected graphics are optional supporting views, never required.

principles: Every requirement is binding once the blueprint is approved.
Build a coherent, high-functioning primate city across all listed domains; no area may be a decorative placeholder where its operation affects play.

Police is the deepest fully simulated institution. Other city systems must function sufficiently and coherently to create, support, constrain and respond to police activity; do not silently expand every institution to equal police-simulation depth.
Preserve meaningful detail. Compress structure, not meaning.
Every persistent entity has a stable unique ID, lifecycle, provenance and explicit relationships.
Time, population, money, stock, capacity, authority and physical location must reconcile across systems.
All generated facts must respect canon, causality, schedules, geography, resources and prior records.
Player actions and decisions remain authoritative; do not auto-solve cases or reveal concealed case truth.
No simulation time advances while the player is out of the simulation.
Do not mark work complete without implementation and test evidence.

divisions.name: Sovereignty, jurisdiction and constitutional order
req: Define Saltwater's sovereign status, territory boundary, jurisdiction, institutions, powers, succession and constitutional rules.
Define legal hierarchy, authority sources, emergency powers, separation of functions and jurisdictional limits.
Prevent external-city or territorial expansion.
tests: Every location resolves inside the single Saltwater jurisdiction or is explicitly marked off-map.
No institution exercises undefined authority.

divisions.name: Geography, land and spatial reference
req: Maintain canonical districts, neighbourhoods, zones, parcels, addresses, coordinates, boundaries, terrain, coastlines and land use.
All places, routes, incidents and properties resolve to consistent spatial IDs.
Support textual descriptions and optional map rendering.
tests: No duplicate or contradictory canonical locations.
Every operational location is addressable and spatially related.

divisions.name: Population accounting and demographic model
req: Enforce the 9,500 opening total: 9,000 residents plus 500 police; 500 reserve; 10,000 hard cap.
Maintain one authoritative person registry and exact living/deceased/entered/exited status.
Track age, household, residence, occupation, eligibility, movement, births, deaths and permanent departures according to canon.
Use atomic capacity checks for arrivals and births; reject any event that would exceed cap.
Prevent double-counting police or people with multiple roles.
tests: Population ledger reconciles to person records.
No valid operation can produce 10,001 living persons.
Police count is a subset of total population, not an extra uncounted population.

divisions.name: Person identity and life records
req: Give each person a stable identity, attributes, history, needs, schedule, skills, employment, finances, relationships and relevant records.
Use tiered processing without deleting or downgrading persistent identities or established facts.
Promote any person materially connected to police activity or a case to persistent full-detail status for the remainder of the simulation.
tests: Identity remains stable across jobs, addresses and relationships.
Promoted people are never downgraded or erased.

divisions.name: Households, relationships and social networks
req: Represent households, families, partners, dependants, friendships, conflicts, professional links and social networks.
Track relationship history, shared addresses, contact patterns and plausible changes.
Generate consistent witness, victim, suspect and community connections without deterministic shortcuts.
tests: Relationship links are reciprocal where applicable and historically traceable.

divisions.name: Housing, property and tenancy
req: Represent residential and commercial parcels, owners, landlords, tenants, leases, occupancy, vacancies, access rights, maintenance and disputes.
Track lease terms, renewals, payments, subletting, licences, keys and occupancy history where relevant.
Ensure occupancy and access facts are time-valid.
tests: No simultaneous incompatible occupancy or ownership state without an explicit explanation.

divisions.name: Businesses and commercial economy
req: Maintain a dedicated business registry with stable IDs, sector, premises, ownership, operators, employees, opening hours, finances, assets, services and lifecycle.
Represent supply, demand, customers, contracts, inventory, deliveries, debts, closures and commercial relationships at a functional level.
Ensure businesses create realistic employment, premises access, records, witnesses, transactions and police-relevant activity.
Avoid mass-generated indistinguishable businesses; maintain coherent variety and traceable ownership.
tests: Every active business has a valid status, sector and location or explicit mobile/virtual basis.
Business employment and premises occupancy reconcile.

divisions.name: Employment, labour and professional life
req: Track jobs, employers, contracts, shifts, attendance, payroll, leave, skills, qualifications, discipline and separation.
Generate plausible work schedules and movement between work and home.
Link employment to businesses, public institutions and police staffing.
tests: A person's simultaneous shifts and locations do not conflict without recorded explanation.

divisions.name: Markets, trade, supply chains and logistics
req: Model essential goods, wholesalers, retailers, imports, exports, ports or gateways if canon establishes them, warehouses, transport and distribution.
Track stock, orders, shortages, deliveries, contracts and disruptions at a proportionate level.
Use coherent off-map dependencies without creating additional playable territory.
tests: Inventory and delivery events reconcile across sender, carrier and receiver.

divisions.name: Public finance, taxation and economic accounts
req: Define currency, public revenue, taxation, fees, expenditure, budgets, debt, grants and financial periods.
Represent business and household finances at a level needed for city function and police cases.
Maintain arithmetic and audit trails; avoid fabricated unbalanced totals.
tests: Every posted transaction balances under its accounting model.

divisions.name: Government and public administration
req: Define executive, legislative, administrative and oversight functions, offices, incumbents, mandates, decision processes and records.
Represent public policy, procurement, permits, licensing, inspections and public complaints.
Ensure government actions have accountable actors, authority and dates.
tests: Every official action has an authorised actor and traceable record.

divisions.name: Civil registry and public records
req: Maintain civil status, identity, address, property, business, permits and other canonically required registers.
Track corrections, versions, issuing authority, access and provenance.
Support lawful in-world retrieval and controlled disclosure.
tests: Record changes preserve prior values and reason for change.

divisions.name: Healthcare and public health
req: Represent hospitals, clinics, practitioners, emergency care, capacity, appointments, treatment events and public-health alerts.
Model injuries, deaths, medical evidence and care access consistently without turning healthcare into a separate deep simulation.
Protect sensitive information through role-based access in-world.
tests: Medical timelines and capacity are internally consistent.

divisions.name: Education, training and research
req: Represent schools, colleges, training providers, enrolment, attendance, staff, qualifications, schedules and facilities.
Support police recruitment/training and city workforce development.
Generate credible education and qualification histories.
tests: Qualifications have issuing bodies, dates and valid prerequisites where applicable.

divisions.name: Social care, welfare and community support
req: Represent social services, housing support, safeguarding, disability support, youth and elder services, charities and community organisations.
Track referrals, eligibility, capacity, case status and outcomes proportionately.
Allow these services to affect vulnerability, risk, support and police interactions.
tests: Referrals have an origin, receiving service, status and outcome or pending state.

divisions.name: Utilities, energy and communications infrastructure
req: Represent water, electricity, sanitation, waste, telecoms, internet and critical infrastructure assets, operators, capacity, outages and restoration.
Model service dependencies and disruption effects on residents, businesses and police.
Track maintenance, incidents and service notices.
tests: Outages affect only connected areas/assets and resolve through recorded restoration.

divisions.name: Roads, transport and mobility
req: Maintain roads, paths, junctions, restrictions, public transport, fleet, routes, timetables, stops, parking and accessibility.
Track person and vehicle movement with plausible travel times and route constraints.
Support dispatch, pursuit, traffic enforcement, emergency access and case timelines.
tests: Travel times and route feasibility are spatially consistent.

divisions.name: Buildings, facilities and physical assets
req: Represent public buildings, private premises, infrastructure, floor plans where needed, entrances, exits, rooms, access controls and asset condition.
Track keys, locks, alarms, maintenance, ownership and authorised access.
Ensure scene geometry and access timelines are internally consistent.
tests: Every access event resolves to a real access point, actor or explainable mechanism.

divisions.name: Environment, weather and natural hazards
req: Model local weather, daylight, tides or water conditions where geographically relevant, seasons, pollution and hazards.
Apply environmental conditions to visibility, travel, infrastructure, health and evidence persistence where justified.
Keep environmental chronology consistent.
tests: Environmental facts are location- and time-valid.

divisions.name: Food systems and essential services
req: Represent food production or procurement, storage, distribution, retail, waste and emergency supply.
Track essential service capacity, disruption and recovery.
Ensure shortages and public effects follow plausible supply constraints.
tests: Essential supply states reconcile across stock and delivery records.

divisions.name: Culture, media, recreation and civic life
req: Represent media outlets, public communications, events, venues, sports, religious/cultural organisations and community gatherings as relevant to canon.
Generate schedules, attendance, public narratives and records that can affect incidents and investigations.
Keep organisations distinct and appropriately scoped.
tests: Events have a time, place, organiser and plausible attendance.

divisions.name: Emergency services and civil protection
req: Define fire/rescue, ambulance, coast or other locally relevant emergency response, disaster coordination and mutual aid within the canon.
Track units, staffing, dispatch, equipment, incidents and interagency handoffs.
Coordinate major incidents without displacing police as the primary deep simulation.
tests: Resource availability and response chronology reconcile across agencies.

divisions.name: Police service governance and structure
req: Define police mandate, command hierarchy, ranks, grades, positions, authority, powers, clearance, divisions, units and reporting lines as separate concepts.
Maintain approximately 500 individually recorded police personnel within the 10,000 population cap.
Define appointment, promotion, transfer, acting roles, succession, discipline, grievance, standards and retirement rules.
Police service must be alive, internally coherent and operationally functional.
tests: Every officer has one authoritative personnel record and valid command/position relationships.

divisions.name: Police personnel and career simulation
req: Track each officer's identity, history, recruitment, vetting, training, qualifications, health/fitness where relevant, skills, performance, welfare, leave, shifts, pay, discipline and career.
Support recruit entry and career progression through vacancies, standards and required training.
Ensure deployments can reflect organisational need while respecting authority, competence and constraints.
tests: No officer performs a role beyond recorded competence/authority without a valid exception.

divisions.name: Police duty rosters, staffing and deployment
req: Generate and maintain shifts, duty rosters, leave, absences, minimum staffing, specialist availability, patrol areas and command coverage.
Account for workload, geography, skills, fatigue and emergency demand.
Record roster changes and actual attendance separately.
tests: No officer is simultaneously assigned to incompatible duties.

divisions.name: Police command, policy and internal governance
req: Represent orders, policies, briefings, operational plans, supervision, approvals, audits, complaints, misconduct and review.
Record who authorised, issued, received and executed every material instruction.
Support fair internal process and traceable decisions.
tests: Material command decisions have authority, rationale and audit trail.

divisions.name: 911, call-taking, CAD and dispatch
req: Represent emergency/non-emergency intake, caller identity or anonymity, call recording, triage, incident creation, unit recommendation, dispatch, radio, status and closure.
Preserve original call content and event chronology; distinguish caller claims from verified facts.
Support concurrent calls, priority changes, escalation and interagency dispatch.
tests: Every dispatched unit and status transition is chronologically auditable.

divisions.name: Patrol, response and field operations
req: Simulate patrol presence, beat coverage, proactive activity, response, scene arrival, dynamic risk, public contact, traffic and field decisions.
Track officer location, availability, equipment and tasking.
Allow routine, complex and unexpected operational events.
tests: Field actions respect time, distance, staffing and available equipment.

divisions.name: Incidents, crime taxonomy and occurrence generation
req: Maintain broad crime and non-crime incident taxonomy with elements, severity, location, victims, suspects, witnesses, methods and reporting routes.
Generate varied, causally grounded incidents across the city and its organisations.
Distinguish occurrence, report, allegation, intelligence, offence and proven finding.
tests: Generated incidents are unique, plausible and linked to valid entities and chronology.

divisions.name: Case management and investigative command
req: Create stable case IDs, ownership, classification, status, objectives, actions, decisions, reviews, deadlines, linked incidents and closure reasons.
Support concurrent investigations, cold cases, linked series, referrals and reopened cases.
Preserve full case chronology and decision provenance.
tests: Every case state change has actor, time, reason and evidence.

divisions.name: Victims, witnesses, suspects and persons of interest
req: Maintain role-specific case links without assuming guilt; track contact, vulnerability, risk, statements, availability and procedural status.
Keep allegation, suspicion, evidential support, charge and finding distinct.
Promote relevant people to persistent full simulation.
tests: No person is treated as guilty solely because of a generated role or suspicion.

divisions.name: Scene management and evidence collection
req: Represent scene boundaries, entry logs, scene security, search areas, recovery methods, exhibits, packaging, seals, handlers and transfers.
Preserve original observations separately from interpretation.
Support physical, digital, documentary, biological, trace and testimonial evidence.
tests: Every exhibit has unique ID, recovery details, continuity and current location/status.

divisions.name: Forensics and specialist examination
req: Represent forensic disciplines, submissions, prioritisation, methods, results, limitations, contamination risks, quality and expert interpretation.
Distinguish raw result, analyst interpretation and investigative inference.
Support specialist resources and realistic turnaround times.
tests: Every conclusion identifies method, source material, limitations and examiner.

divisions.name: Interviews, interrogations and statements
req: Represent interview planning, cautions/procedural status as fictional canon requires, participants, recordings, notes, questions, answers, breaks, disclosure and statement versions.
Preserve verbatim or detailed source content where available; distinguish summaries from originals.
Do not generate leading prompts or reveal hidden case solutions to the player.
tests: Interview chronology, participants and recording references reconcile.

divisions.name: Intelligence, analysis and information handling
req: Represent source grading, reliability, confidence, dissemination, restrictions, analytical products, links and review dates.
Separate intelligence from evidence and established fact.
Preserve source provenance and uncertainty.
tests: Every intelligence item has source, confidence and handling status.

divisions.name: Surveillance, observation and technical monitoring
req: Represent physical observation, CCTV, ANPR or equivalent systems, authorised technical monitoring, coverage, blind spots, time drift, retention and retrieval.
Track requests, authorisations, collection windows, operators, exports and evidential continuity.
Never treat absence of coverage as proof of absence.
tests: Every surveillance item has source device, coverage limits and time basis.

divisions.name: Arrest, search, warrants and custody
req: Represent grounds, authority, applications, approvals, execution, person/property searches, seizure, transport, booking, detention, welfare, reviews and release.
Maintain custody clock and property continuity.
Separate operational action from later legal decision.
tests: Custody and warrant events satisfy configured fictional rules and chronological constraints.

divisions.name: Prosecution, courts and legal outcomes
req: Represent charging decisions, disclosure, prosecution, defence, hearings, evidence, rulings, verdicts, sentencing, appeals and case outcomes.
Track procedural state and legal actors; preserve acquittals, dismissals and unresolved outcomes.
Feed outcomes back into records without rewriting investigative history.
tests: Court outcomes link to the correct charges, defendants and evidence versions.

divisions.name: Corrections, rehabilitation and post-sentence status
req: Represent sentence execution, prison or community supervision, rehabilitation, release, recall and post-release status proportionately.
Maintain continuity between custody, court and person records.
tests: Sentence and release dates reconcile with court orders.

divisions.name: Complaints, oversight and public accountability
req: Represent public complaints, independent review, internal investigations, inspections, findings, remedies and published outcomes.
Preserve due process, conflicts of interest and auditability.
Allow institutional failure and public trust to evolve from events.
tests: Every complaint has a route, owner, status and outcome or pending reason.

divisions.name: Time, calendar, schedules and simulation clock
req: Maintain one authoritative in-world clock, calendar, time zones, shifts, opening hours, deadlines and event ordering.
No time advances while player is outside the simulation; resume without hidden elapsed simulation time.
Support paused, active, queued and historical events.
tests: All event timestamps use one canonical time basis and stable ordering.

divisions.name: Simulation engine, causality and world activity
req: Coordinate people, organisations, services, incidents, schedules, resources, weather and time through deterministic, auditable event processing where feasible.
Use relevance-based processing without breaking persistence or continuity.
Prevent impossible simultaneous states, causal loops and unexplained state mutation.
Background activity must not advance while the player is out.
tests: Replay of a recorded event sequence yields the same authoritative state where deterministic replay is specified.

divisions.name: AI generation, narrative and player agency
req: Generate detailed, varied, naturalistic text consistent with records, knowledge boundaries, character voice and uncertainty.
Separate hidden world truth from player-visible information and from NPC knowledge.
Never disclose culprit/accomplice/perpetrator identities or hidden solution unless the player types exactly 'bingo'.
Never provide unsolicited solution hints or tell the player what to investigate next; present available records and let the player decide.
All generated claims that alter canon must be persisted as structured events or records.
tests: No hidden truth leaks before the exact reveal trigger.
NPC knowledge never exceeds their plausible information.

divisions.name: Text interface, commands and player workflow
req: Provide a laptop-style, text-first interface with clear navigation, commands, records, status and contextual actions.
Support individual-officer gameplay, including recruit start where selected.
Keep prose and source records readable while using compact presentation for navigation and metadata.
No essential action depends on graphics.
tests: All essential workflows are operable through text commands and views.

divisions.name: Maps, diagrams and visual evidence
req: Provide optional maps, layouts, timelines, charts and forensic scene visuals when useful or requested.
Visuals must derive from canonical spatial/evidence data and never silently contradict text records.
Keep text as authoritative source.
tests: Every visual can be traced to the underlying canonical records.

divisions.name: Database, schemas and persistence
req: Use Neon PostgreSQL as the persistent database and GitHub as source control, specification and migration history; ChatGPT is the user-facing AI partner/interface.
Define canonical schemas, constraints, relationships, IDs, migrations, indexes and transaction boundaries.
Store detailed narrative losslessly; normalise shared facts, reference repeated entities and avoid duplicate payloads.
Separate immutable source records/events from derived views and summaries.
Never claim live database connectivity without a successful connection test.
tests: Schema constraints enforce identity, referential integrity, population cap and valid lifecycle states.

divisions.name: Storage efficiency and capacity governance
req: Use compact keys, enums, references, normalisation, deduplication and lossless compression where justified; compress structure, never meaningful narrative.
Avoid redundant fields, duplicate text, unnecessary indexes, repeated snapshots and unbounded logs.
Measure row, table, index and TOAST growth; benchmark representative high-entropy long text.

Before every Neon migration, schema change, seed/import, bulk write or upload, show current measured baseline, incremental estimate in bytes and MB/MiB, method, assumptions, uncertainty range and projected total; wait for explicit user approval.
After approved deployment, measure actual growth and compare with estimate. If estimate is not credible, benchmark first; do not deploy.
tests: No Neon write occurs without explicit approval after a documented estimate.
Post-deployment measured delta is recorded.

divisions.name: Security, permissions and information boundaries
req: Define user, player, officer, administrator and system roles; least privilege; secret handling; access checks and audit logs.
Protect hidden case truth and restricted personal information from player-facing leakage.
Keep credentials out of source control, narrative records and logs.
tests: Unauthorised reads/writes are rejected and audited.

divisions.name: Backups, recovery and data integrity
req: Define backup cadence, retention, restore testing, point-in-time recovery where available, export format and disaster recovery procedure.
Protect canon and authoritative records against corruption, accidental overwrite and partial writes.
Keep recoverable backups separate from live mutable state.
tests: A tested restore reproduces a verified checkpoint.

divisions.name: Testing, validation and simulation quality
req: Maintain unit, integration, schema, migration, end-to-end, replay, load, population, storage and narrative-quality tests.
Test edge cases, adversarial inputs, boundary conditions, race conditions, long-running continuity and cross-system reconciliation.
Use evidence-based completion criteria and regression gates.
tests: Every division has traceable acceptance tests and recorded results.

divisions.name: Operations, observability and maintenance
req: Track service health, errors, latency, job queues, resource use, database size, failed events and recovery actions.
Provide safe maintenance, migration, rollback and incident procedures.
Separate development/test data from authoritative simulation data.
tests: Operational failures are detectable, attributable and recoverable.

divisions.name: Canon, versioning and change control
req: Maintain a single canonical blueprint version, decision log, glossary, schema registry and traceability matrix.
No unapproved changes to canon, division structure, requirements or approved design.
Record every amendment with reason, approval, affected requirements, migration impact and tests.
Keep proposed, approved, implemented, verified and retired states distinct.
tests: Every implementation item maps to an approved requirement and evidence.

cross_cutting.rule: Stable identity and provenance across every domain.
Single source of truth; no contradictory duplicate authority.
All time-dependent facts are effective-dated and historically queryable.
All financial, population, inventory, staffing and capacity changes reconcile.
Distinguish fact, allegation, estimate, inference, intelligence and opinion.
Preserve originals; derived summaries never replace source records.
No hidden simulation time while player is out.
Text-first operation; optional visuals cannot be required.
Police receives deepest simulation; all other domains remain operationally coherent and connected.
No implementation marked complete without reproducible evidence.

completion_rule: A division is VERIFIED only when its requirements are implemented, acceptance tests pass, cross-system dependencies are reconciled, and evidence is linked in GitHub. Documentation alone is not implementation.
change_control: The user owns canon and final approval. Do not add, remove, reorder, rename, split, merge or materially reinterpret divisions without explicit approval. Keep all changes versioned and traceable.
out_of_scope: A second playable city or external territory
Equal-depth simulation of every non-police institution
Graphics as a prerequisite for gameplay
traceability: Every requirement receives a stable requirement ID derived from division ID and sequence; each implementation, test, schema object and evidence record references those IDs.
